subtopics.title: Continental Drift and the Evidence for It

questions.question: The single supercontinent proposed by Wegener, and its two fragments, were:
options: Gondwana, splitting into Pangaea and Laurasia
Pangaea, splitting into Laurasia in the north and Gondwana in the south
Laurasia, splitting into Pangaea and Gondwana
Panthalassa, splitting into Africa and Asia

questions.question: Why is Mesosaurus such strong evidence for continental drift?
options: It was a freshwater reptile that could not cross an ocean, yet its fossils occur in both the Karoo and South America
It was a flying reptile that could migrate between continents
It lived only in Antarctica
Its fossils are found only in Africa

questions.question: The Dwyka tillite in South Africa is climatic evidence for drift because it shows that:
options: The Karoo was once a warm swamp
Sea levels were once much higher
A continental ice sheet once covered land that now has a hot climate, matching glacial deposits on other continents
Volcanic ash once buried the region

questions.question: Wegener's theory was rejected for half a century mainly because:
options: His fossil evidence was proved false
The coastlines did not actually fit
Nobody had mapped the ocean floor
He could not explain what force moved the continents

subtopics.title: The Engine — Convection Currents and Sea-Floor Spreading

questions.question: Convection currents in the mantle are driven by:
options: Heat from radioactive decay and from the earth's formation, making hot rock rise and cooler rock sink
The pull of the moon on the ocean floor
Wind stress on the continents
Rainwater seeping into the crust

questions.question: Which statement about the mantle is CORRECT?
options: It is a global ocean of liquid lava
It is solid rock that flows plastically at a few centimetres a year
It is a gas layer under pressure
It is frozen solid and does not move at all

questions.question: Slab pull refers to:
options: New crust sliding off the raised mid-ocean ridge
Wind dragging plates westward
The weight of a cold, dense sinking plate hauling the rest of the plate behind it
Continents pulling oceans closed

questions.question: Magnetic striping on the ocean floor proves sea-floor spreading because the stripes are:
options: Randomly scattered across the whole ocean
Only found next to the continents
Identical everywhere on earth
Parallel to the ridge and mirrored symmetrically on both sides of it

questions.question: Divergent boundaries are also called constructive boundaries because:
options: New crust is created there as magma rises and solidifies
Buildings are safest there
They construct deep ocean trenches
They join two continents together

questions.question: The East African Rift Valley is best described as:
options: A single deep canyon cut by a river
A broad flat-floored valley walled by fault scarps, holding long deep lakes, with volcanoes along the fractures
A ridge of folded mountains raised by compression
A chain of volcanic islands rising from the sea floor

questions.question: At a transform (conservative) boundary you would NOT expect to find:
options: Shallow, violent earthquakes
A long straight fault line
Volcanoes
Streams and fences offset sideways

questions.question: Earthquakes at mid-ocean ridges are shallow and moderate because:
options: The ocean water absorbs the energy
No plates actually move there
The magma is too cold to fracture
The crust there is thin, hot and weak, so it cannot store large amounts of strain

questions.question: Oceanic crust subducts beneath continental crust because it is:
options: Denser, at about 3,0 g/cm³ against about 2,7 g/cm³
Thicker than continental crust
Older than the mantle
Softer and more easily bent

questions.question: The Peru-Chile Trench and the Andes were produced by:
options: Two continental plates colliding
The Nazca oceanic plate subducting beneath the South American continental plate
A transform fault sliding past the coast
A mid-ocean ridge splitting the continent

questions.question: Continental-continental collision such as India into Eurasia produces:
options: Deep trenches and island arcs
Rift valleys and shield volcanoes
Very high fold mountains and powerful earthquakes, but essentially no volcanoes
New oceanic crust and magnetic striping

questions.question: South Africa records few natural earthquakes mainly because:
options: Its rocks are too young to fracture
It has no fault lines of any kind
The Cape Fold Mountains absorb the shaking
It lies near the middle of the African plate, far from any plate boundary

questions.question: In the torn-newspaper comparison, the 'sentences running across the tear' stand for:
options: The shape of the coastlines only
Matching fossils, rocks and glacial deposits that continue from one continent onto another
The width of the Atlantic Ocean
The names given to the continents

questions.question: Glossopteris supports drift because its seeds were:
options: Carried by ocean currents to every continent
Poisonous to sea creatures
Too heavy to be blown across an ocean, yet the plant grew on five now-separated landmasses
Only ever found in Antarctica

questions.question: The Cape Fold Mountains are geological evidence for drift because they:
options: Contain fossils of sea creatures
Are the oldest mountains on earth
Run from north to south instead of east to west
Continue, with the same age and folding, in Argentina and Antarctica

questions.question: In the pot-on-the-stove comparison, the 'skin of cooled porridge' represents:
options: The lithosphere — crust plus the rigid top of the mantle, about 100 km thick
The liquid outer core
The atmosphere
The asthenosphere only

questions.question: The 'tablecloth sliding off the table' describes which force?
options: Ridge push
Slab pull
Erosion
Isostasy

questions.question: The age of the ocean floor supports spreading because it is:
options: The same age everywhere
Oldest at the ridge and youngest at the continents
Youngest at the ridge, older toward the continents, and nowhere older than about 200 million years
Always older than the continents

questions.question: Roughly how fast do plates move?
options: Several metres per day
About a kilometre per year
They do not move measurably
A few centimetres per year — about as fast as fingernails grow

questions.question: Two taxis squeezing past each other side by side illustrates which boundary?
options: Transform (conservative)
Divergent (constructive)
Convergent (destructive)
Subduction zone

questions.question: Where two oceanic plates converge, the landform produced is:
options: A continental rift valley
A trench with a curved island arc of volcanic islands, as at Japan
A mid-ocean ridge with fissure eruptions
A straight fault with offset streams

questions.question: Which boundary neither creates nor destroys crust?
options: Divergent
Oceanic-continental convergent
Transform
Continental-continental convergent

questions.question: The Ring of Fire is a belt of volcanoes and earthquakes that traces:
options: The equator
The mid-Atlantic ridge
The East African Rift
The subduction boundaries encircling the Pacific Ocean
